title: OpenAPI describes provider routes as the server behaves: rate-limit 429s, empty likes cursor and long q
acceptance: Every /providers/* route whose spec reuses the Spotify-quota 429 (search, playlists, track-import, playlist-import, likes) also documents its per-user rate-limit 429: the RATE_LIMITED error code and the Retry-After header from lib/rate-limit.ts, so a client can tell a short wait from PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Limit values come from the limiter config rather than duplicated literals, or are stated once in api.md.
The likes cursor parameter states minLength 1 (the server answers an empty ?cursor= with 422), or the server treats an empty cursor as the first page; the spec and the code agree.

q on likes and on catalog search matches the server: either over-200 q is rejected with 422, or the spec says q is truncated to 200. The likes rate limiter and handler use the same trimmed and truncated q, so a padded q cannot spend the search budget and then return an unfiltered page.
OpenAPI is regenerated, drift and contract-parity pass, and a later iOS PR refreshes web-contract/ (workspace rule: web first).
nextAction: Spun out of RF-156 (iOS #52 final review, 2026-10-31; scope widened by the #674 review). evidence.summary: Final review of iOS #52 (snapshot of web 0a77110), items 1-3: the likes 429 omits the per-user rate limits; cursor lacks minLength though the server rejects empty; q maxLength 200 while the server truncates.
Web record PR that created this record.

Final review of #674: the 429 mismatch is the shared Spotify-quota 429 on all provider routes; RATE_LIMITED and Retry-After are undocumented; catalog search q is also silently truncated; the likes limiter trims q before truncation; generate-openapi.ts is owner-gated too.
